scenes.title: Explain the proposed value
scenes.visual: Founder reviews an anonymous opportunity statement.
scenes.narration: Your opportunity describes an improvement worth investigating. A value proposition describes the benefit you propose for a specific group, how you might help, and why that approach could matter. It is a hypothesis, not a slogan, proven advantage or guarantee.

scenes.title: Benefit before features
scenes.narration: A feature describes what an approach does. A benefit describes the useful outcome for the person. A location pin is a feature; clearer directions to registration is a possible benefit. Do not invent time saved, reduced costs or guaranteed satisfaction without evidence.

scenes.title: Choose a provisional approach
scenes.visual: Illustrative visitor follows clearly arranged information.
scenes.narration: Describe a simple approach that might deliver the benefit. It could be a service, process, physical information or digital tool. The choice is provisional. Do not assume an app is best, and do not turn a long feature list into a promise of value.

scenes.title: Compare with current alternatives
scenes.visual: Editable current approach and proposed approach cards.
scenes.narration: What already helps people, and what reason might they have to try something different? Record a possible difference fairly, with its evidence status. Include learning, trust, effort and other switching burdens. If there is no credible reason to change, revise the proposition.

scenes.title: Write a claim you can check
scenes.visual: Editable customer, benefit, approach and evidence cards.
scenes.narration: For this group in this situation, we propose this approach to help achieve this benefit. Compared with the current approach, our possible difference is this hypothesis. We still need to check this uncertainty. Keep user and possible buyer roles separate, and do not claim willingness to pay.

scenes.title: Draft and test understanding
scenes.narration: Create your Value Proposition Draft and Test Plan. Include the group, benefit, approach, alternatives, possible difference, evidence limits, plain-language statement and next check. You can first check whether people understand it, but clarity is not demand, adoption or payment proof.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Describe value in the customer’s terms.

children: A
value proposition
explains the benefit you propose for a specific group, your provisional approach and a possible reason to choose it. It is not proof of demand or a marketing guarantee.
Feature
What an approach does: a location pin, printed map or staff handover.
Benefit
The useful outcome: clearer directions to registration. The importance and effectiveness still need checking.
Possible difference
A reason your approach might matter compared with current options. Treat it as a hypothesis unless supported.
Evidence limit
What is known, assumed or planned. Do not fabricate metrics, testimonials or superiority.
Illustrative draft:

“For first-time visitors seeking registration, we propose clearly arranged directions to help locate the correct desk. A possible difference is easier access to relevant information; usefulness and switching burden remain untested.” This is a hypothesis, not a proven claim.
Write a plain-language draft
State the group and situation, including user versus possible buyer.
Name the benefit rather than a feature list.
Describe one provisional approach, with limits.
Compare fairly with the current alternative.
Label the possible difference and evidence gaps.
Choose a check that can change the draft.

Checking whether someone understands the statement tests clarity. A polite reaction, preference or clear explanation does not establish adoption, switching or payment. Keep those questions separate for later evidence gathering.
Review opportunity statement
Review landscape map

Simulated Coach · no AI connection
Try four scripted guidance modes. The preview reads your current worksheet locally; it does not send information anywhere.

replies.teach: A value proposition links a specific group, benefit, provisional approach and possible reason to choose it. Benefits are outcomes, not feature lists.
replies.guide: Compare your draft with current alternatives. Label the possible difference, switching burden and evidence gaps; choose a fair next check.
replies.review: Value Proposition check: {missing} required fields still empty. This scripted check counts fields only; it cannot verify benefits, superiority, adoption or demand.
replies.challenge: Is the benefit a feature? Are promises sourced? Does the workaround already suffice? Are you confusing comprehension or polite preference with payment?
